subject: Three level hierarchical regression model with multivariate priors

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: Three level hierarchical regression model with multivariate priors
parts:
Hello stan users,


I am wondering how to adapt the example from section 5.11. (Multivariate Priors for Hierarchical Models: Optimization through Cholesky Factorization) in the stan reference (pages 56/57) to a situation with three levels, e.g. individuals nested in schools, which are nested in school districts.

So far I have formulated a model in which I implement

(A) Hyper priors, i.e. mean and sd of a normal distribution for regression weights
(B) Top level (i.e. school district level) estimates of regression weights drawn from (A).
(C) Next level (i.e. school level) estimates of regression weights drawn from (B).

Here, (C) plays the role the parameter “gamma” plays in the stan reference example.

I have not changed how the covariance of regression weights is modeled, meaning that I assume that it is the same for all groups, which is a reasonable assumption for my data.

The model (code below) compiles and produces reasonable results, but the number of effective sample is not great. The lowest n_eff is around 3% of the total post-warmup samples when fitting a toy model with 12 groups—3 top level groups, each with 4 next level groups—, N = 900, 7000 warmup samples and 3000 post warmup samples, most n_eff are around 30-40% of the post warm up samples.

My questions are:

- Does the general approach to model the multiple nested levels seem reasonable? 
- Do you have any suggestions as to how to improve the model?



I’d appreciate any comment that points out problems with my intended approach before I run the modelwith all data :-)

Cheers - Guido



################## model ######################
data {
  int<lower=1> N;               // number of data points
  real<lower=0> y[N];           // observations
  int M;                        // total number of groups
  int M1;                       // number of top level groups
  int MtoM1[M];                 // indicator to which of the top level group a nect level group belongs
  int<lower=1, upper M>  g[N];  // group for individual
  int<lower=1> K;               // number parameters
  matrix[N,K] x;                // individual predictors
}


parameters {
  matrix[M,K] z;
  cholesky_factor_corr[K] L_Omega; 
  vector<lower=0>[K] tau;                 // prior scale
  vector[K] hyper_gamma;                  // group coeffs
  vector<lower=0>[K] hyper_gamma_scale;   // group coeffs
  matrix[M1,K] gamma;                     // mean beta values for top level groups
}


transformed parameters {
  matrix[M,K] beta; 
  for (m in 1:M) {
    beta[m] <- gamma[MtoM1[m]] + (diag_pre_multiply(tau,L_Omega) * z[m]')';
  }
}


model {
  vector[N] raysig; 
  tau ~ cauchy(0,2.5);
  to_vector(z) ~ normal(0,1);
  L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
  to_vector(hyper_gamma) ~ normal(0,5); // mean of top level groups
  to_vector(hyper_gamma_scale) ~ cauchy(0,2.5); // sd of top level groups
 

  // sample mean parameters for top level groups from "hyper prior"
  for (k in 1:K) {
    for (g1 in 1:M1) {
      gamma[g1,k] ~ normal(hyper_gamma[k],hyper_gamma_scale[k]);  
    }
  }


  for (n in 1:N) {
    // note: using the (faster) rayleigh here as stand-in 
    // for a (slower) poisson/negative binomial model to be used later
    raysig[n] <- exp(dot_product(x[n],beta[g[n]]));
    }
  y ~ rayleigh(raysig);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Three level hierarchical regression model with multivariate priors
parts:
The best thing you can do for efficiency in this kind of case
is use the non-centered parameterization for gamma. You can keep doing
it up the hierarchy.

I don't know the Rayleigh, but if you use something like negative
binomial, you can take a log-scale parameter, which should be more stable.

I don't know how big the arrays are, but you can rewrite this

column(gamma, k) ~ normal(hyper_gamma[k], hyper_gamma_scale[k]);

and if M1 is large, you get a fairly big speedup in this operation.

You might want to make the transformed parameter a local parameter in
the model to avoid writing it out or saving it.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Three level hierarchical regression model with multivariate priors
parts:
Thanks Bob!

One issue popped up: you had written column instead of of col.
it should be

col(gamma, k) ~ normal(hyper_gamma[k], hyper_gamma_scale[k]); 

when I use this version I get the following warning message:
"
DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal): Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) contains a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variabl                                            e.
 You must call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
  Sampling Statement left-hand-side expression:
    col(gamma,k) ~ normal_log(...)
"

This warning is not shown when I use 2 loops instead.

Is there a reason the warning shows only up when I sample parameters for an entire column?

Guido

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Three level hierarchical regression model with multivariate priors
parts:
The warning appears every time there is a function used on the left hand side of a sampling expression, whether it actually needs a Jacobson adjustment.

In this case, col() does not require an adjustment, so it it's safe to ignore the warning.

Daniel
